seo_description: How Lanevia turns dash cam footage into de-identified road data: record, detect, confirm, share by consent, and pay drivers back.
title: From your windshield to safer roads
intro: Every RoadSense One follows the same five steps. Nothing is shared unless a driver said yes to that buyer, at that data level.

steps.title: Record
steps.text: The front-facing camera records the road ahead. Audio is off by default, and faces and plates are blurred on the device.

steps.title: Detect
steps.text: The on-device model flags road conditions such as work zones and closures, with a location, time and confidence score.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.text: An event is released only after 3 or more different cameras see it on the same stretch of road that day, so it describes the road, not a person.

steps.title: Share by consent
steps.text: Data goes to a buyer only if the driver opted in for that buyer and data level, under a signed license that bans re-identification.

steps.title: Pay it back
steps.text: Each month, 25% of license revenue is split across the drivers whose data was used and applied as a bill credit.

levels.name: Detection
levels.receives: Road-segment event: type, segment, time window, confidence

levels.name: Blurred clip
levels.receives: Event clip with faces and plates blurred on the device

levels.name: Raw video
levels.receives: Unblurred video, for government requests with legal process only

levels.name: Trip trace
levels.receives: Trip sequences from one camera; blocked by our de-identification rules

privacy: We never sell to credit reporting agencies.
Buyers never receive customer, device or clip IDs, or a sequence of events from one camera.
Every license contract prohibits re-identifying drivers.
We do not sell location data for drivers in states that ban it.
Insurers and data brokers receive aggregate road data only.
